card.name: Linking words before co-use or co-infection
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as and, with, when, or part of concomitant, right after a drug or co-infection is named. They come just before a second drug, a second condition, or a change in therapy.

modes.label: Co-infection phrase
modes.description: The word and or part of HBV just after HIV-1 and HBV, before stopping the drug.
modes.example: have been reported in patients who are coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV<< and>> have discontinued EMTRIVA or VIRE

modes.label: Concomitant or co-administered use
modes.description: Linking word or part of concomitant, with or when, that leads into a second drug in an interaction statement.
modes.example: The blood levels of tacrolimus may increase upon concom<<itant>> use with cannabidiol. When

card.writes: It favors 'when' and similar linking words, and suppresses 'success' and 'effective' words.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a drug label where a second drug or condition is about to be named alongside the first.
